**Recovery backups.** Cloak can now back up the files a drive can't be opened
without (its header and every folder list) into a password-protected file,
and put them back if they're ever lost or damaged.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.3.0-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.3.0-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again).

## What's new

- **Back up** a drive from the save button on its card, or all drives from
  Settings → Recovery. You get one `.cloakbak` file, protected by a password
  you choose; a wrong password or a damaged backup is detected. It holds the
  drive header (`meta.json`) and every folder list, not your files: keep a
  normal backup of each drive's folder for those, and keep the recovery file
  somewhere other than the drive's own disk.
- **Restore from a backup** (Settings → Recovery) puts a drive's header and
  folder lists back only where they're missing or damaged. Anything that
  still reads is newer than the backup and is left alone, so files added
  since aren't hidden. It needs both the backup's password and the drive's,
  and won't touch an unlocked drive or a folder holding a different drive.
- The same from the command line: `cloak backup`, `cloak backup-list`,
  `cloak restore` (see the README).

## Known limitations

- **The macOS app has not yet been tested on a real Mac.** Treat it as a
  preview and keep a backup of anything you put in a drive.
- A recovery backup is a snapshot: files created after it can't be named
  from it if their folder's list is later lost.
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
